verdict.rationale: Airbyte has a first-party Typing and Deduping docs page. Its quoted text confirms one-to-one table mapping into the warehouse ("No more sub-tables"), which points to structured destination tables rather than raw blobs. However, the quoted spans do not state that columns are typed or that records are deduplicated, and the sync-mode docs do not mention dedup behavior. missing for 10: explicit evidence of typed columns, explicit evidence of deduplication (e.g., a dedup sync mode or primary-key handling), handling of typing errors, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an analytics engineer, loaded data lands as typed, deduplicated destination tables ready to query, not raw JSON blobs

citations.quote: One-to-one table mapping: Data in one stream will always be mapped to one table in your data warehouse. No more sub-tables.
A sync mode governs how Airbyte reads from a source and writes to a destination.
